title: input_parity_demolish omits sel_pipe — zero-value 0 presets 'pipe 0 selected', so the scripted click-select step can never fail the scenario
detail: The scenario promises 'draw, click-select the pipe, X demolishes it', but the omitted sel_pipe zero-value 0 flows verbatim into the executor surface, where -1 (not 0) means none and >= 0 means selected. The X demolish targets pipe 0 even if the mid01 click-select is broken — the selection step is a self-fulfilling pin, and the struct's '0 = none selected' comment is false under executor semantics.
recommended_fix: Set `sel_pipe = -1` on input_parity_demolish so the X gate depends on the scripted click-select; fix the Parity_Scenario field comment to '-1 = none selected' to match inp.init and the executor gates.

title: input_parity_reject selection-unchanged pin uses && — a single-field selection change passes silently
detail: The check promises 'a rejected draw must not change the selection', but the && connective only fails when BOTH sel_node and sel_pipe changed; a regression that changes exactly one (e.g. click_select's junction branch dropping its sel_pipe = -1 reset) stays green.
recommended_fix: Change the condition to `r.sel_node != -1 || r.sel_pipe != -1` so any selection change after the rejected draw fails the scenario.
